chunks: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) said:
And in another hadith, he said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) said:
'Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim. Indeed, Allah loves the seekers of knowledge.'

key_terms.بُغَاةَ الْعِلْمِ: Seekers of knowledge — those who actively pursue learning. The root b-gh-y in this context carries the sense of earnest, purposeful seeking.
key_terms.طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ: Seeking/pursuing knowledge — an active endeavor, not passive reception. In classical Islamic scholarship, 'ilm encompassed religious, ethical, and practical knowledge.
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: A religious obligation of the highest category — the same word used for the five daily prayers and other obligatory duties (fara'id). Its use here elevates seeking knowledge to a fundamental duty.

ai.seo_question: Is seeking knowledge obligatory in Islam according to hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a chain ending with Imam al-Sadiq (AS), reports the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) declaring that the pursuit of knowledge is a religious obligation (farida) for every Muslim. The second version adds that Allah Himself loves those who actively seek knowledge, elevating the pursuit of learning to both a duty and a path to divine love. This teaching was particularly significant in early Islamic society, where it countered tendencies toward religious stagnation and encouraged believers to actively engage with scholarship.
